subject: Throughput safeguard measurement and tiered discount ask
messages:
From: Lina Torres <lina.torres@acmedatalabs.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmedatalabs.com
Date: 2027-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Throughput guarantees + measurement plan 

Hi Karthik / Ben,

Quick follow from our procurement call — Acme needs firm throughput guarantees for any Dedicated (reserved) GPU pool we sign up for. Specifically: a tokens/sec commitment and a requests/sec SLA, plus latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99). Our security and procurement teams will run an acceptance test during the onboarding window, and pricing will hinge on how you define the acceptance criteria and how we measure it.

Can you provide: 1) a clear measurement methodology your team will accept, 2) what you consider a passing result for tokens/sec and requests/sec, and 3) how pricing/discounts map to committed throughput bands? We want to avoid ambiguous guarantees and minimize post-deployment disputes.

Also, please attach any test harness or scripts you expect us to run and any minimum warmup / KV-cache assumptions.

Thanks — Lina
Lina Torres
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Data Labs
procurement@acmedatalabs.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Lina Torres <lina.torres@acmedatalabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T13:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput guarantees + measurement plan

Thanks Lina — high level answer up front, then a proposed acceptance protocol below. Happy to jump on a short call to walk the team through the details.

Summary upfront: Redwood can provide committed throughput guarantees expressed in sustained tokens/sec and requests/sec over a defined test window. Pricing discounts for Dedicated commits will be tiered by committed sustained tokens/sec (or equivalent GPU-commit band). Acceptance is a pass/fail run using Redwood's validated harness; failures below the agreed threshold trigger remediation timeframes and pro-rated credits (not immediate termination).

Proposed measurement methodology (short):
- Definitions:
  - tokens/sec: aggregate decoded tokens per second observed at the Redwood edge during steady-state (post-warmup).
  - requests/sec: count of incoming inference requests completed per second. For multi-turn chat we use request-level completion (end-of-stream) as the event.
- Test workload profile:
  - We recommend a 60-minute sustained test window. First 5 minutes = warmup (no scoring). Next 50 minutes = measurement. Final 5 minutes = cool-down.
  - Sequence length distribution: we'll provide a sample trace that matches your production mix (we expect ~70% short <64 tokens, 25% mid 64–512, 5% long >512). If you want a different mix, we can encode that into the harness.
  - KV-cache behavior: tests should be run both cold (no KV cache) and warm (KV hits simulated) if you rely on context re-use. We accept separate pass thresholds for cold vs warm runs.
- Environment and controls:
  - Test runs must be executed from the agreed test client (we'll provide a VM image and script). Network egress from your side should use the test IP ranges we agree on to avoid noisy neighbor on your network path.
  - Model pinned: acceptance runs must use the production model and exact model version you will serve (we will pin a digest/version).
- Metrics and pass criteria:
  - Primary: median tokens/sec across the 50-minute measurement window must be >= committed tokens/sec.
  - Secondary: 95th percentile latency (end-to-end per request) must be <= agreed latency target (e.g., 250ms for short requests, 600ms for mid, 1500ms for long).
  - Availability: at least 99.5% of measurement samples must be above 90% of the committed tokens/sec. Any shortfalls must be documented with traces.
  - Requests/sec: average requests/sec must be within +/-10% of the expected requests/sec derived from your traffic mix; we convert committed tokens/sec into requests/sec internally for provisioning but record both for transparency.
- Fail / remediation:
  - If the run fails, Redwood will provide a remediation plan and a follow-up run window within 7 business days. Persistent failure (>=2 failed runs) triggers crediting as per the SLA table in the attached matrix.

Attached: acceptance_test_script.sh (simple harness), and a draft pricing matrix (commit_pricing_matrix.xlsx) mapping commit bands to discounts. I've also linked a short SOC2 summary for procurement.

If that looks ok, Ben can propose specific commit bands and discounts and we can lock an onboarding test window.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lina Torres <lina.torres@acmedatalabs.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput guarantees + measurement plan

Great summary Karthik — adding pricing specifics so Acme can evaluate:

Suggested commit bands (example):
- Band A: 200k sustained tokens/sec -> 20% platform discount + 2% month credit on failure
- Band B: 500k sustained tokens/sec -> 28% platform discount + 5% month credit on failure
- Band C: 1M sustained tokens/sec -> 35% platform discount + 10% month credit on failure

We modeled these against our GPU pool sizing assumptions (attached matrix). If Acme is flexible on exact commit (tokens vs GPU pool sizing), we can map to a guaranteed GPU vCPU allocation and hold the price. Discounts above assume a 12-month reserved commit.

Two asks from our side: 1) confirm your baseline production mix (we included a sample trace in the Drive link), and 2) whether you require cold-run vs warm-run gating (cold-run failures typically require extra provisioning).

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lina Torres <lina.torres@acmedatalabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput guarantees + measurement plan

Hi Lina — looping in procurement checklist and SOW template. Per company policy we need:
- Signed SOW + PO tied to the selected commit band
- Confirmation of test IP ranges (we'll provide firewall rules)
- DOCS: completed SOC2 attestation (attached), data retention statements, and contact for security review

I've attached the proposed SOW (proposed-sow-acme-v3.docx) and a short SOC2 summary for your security team. We'll prep a DocuSign envelope once you confirm band selection.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Lina Torres <lina.torres@acmedatalabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput guarantees + measurement plan

Thanks all — this is exactly what we needed.

Acme will:
- Confirm internal production trace and send the sample by EOD Monday (we want the test to match our 70/25/5 split you called out).
- Target Band B (500k sustained tokens/sec) for the initial commit, pending final pricing confirmation.
- Schedule the acceptance test for Thurs May 28 10:00–11:30 PT. Please reserve that slot and provide the test VM image + script.

We will sign the SOW once we get final pricing and confirm the DocuSign link. For the test, we prefer to gate on the warm-run (KV cache enabled) as that's closest to our real traffic.

Lina
Lina Torres
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Data Labs
